reran: cmd.sh: 'Error while emitting G$ / Index 0 out of bounds for length 0' (ASM Frame.merge in MethodWriter.computeAllFrames) on w4-int and w3-base; 2.13.18 compiles and the class fails with VerifyError: Inconsistent stackmap frames. My ordinary variant P1 (below) is the other way round: VerifyError on w4-int and w3-base, ASM crash on 2.13.18 and on Scala 3.7.4. The 2.13.18 compiler with scala-asm 9.11.1-scala-1 on the class path crashes on G; with 9.10.1-scala-1 it does not.
user_impact: A return evaluated while the enclosing expression has operands on the stack (an argument of a call with a receiver, an operand of +, the right side of += on a field) inside a try/finally that has another return: def m(log: StringBuilder, s: String): Int = try { log.append(if (s == null) return -1 else s); if (s.isEmpty) return 0; s.length } finally println("fin") fails to compile or fails verification depending on the ASM version. The scala/bug#10183 reporter hit it in real code (an assignment through a captured var from a match with a return arm). The finding's getOrElse(return x) example is wrong: a by-name argument puts the return in a closure, which compiles and runs correctly.
fixability: design question: genReturn must drop or spill the operand stack before jumping to the cleanup, which needs the backend to know the stack contents at the return (Scala 3 does this for other jumps out of expressions); the alternative is UnCurry/a pre-backend phase lifting returns out of expression positions inside try/finally. No binary cost either way.
regression: from 2.12 (scala/bug#10183 reports 2.11 compiled the original program; GenBCode since 2.12.0). Not a draft-fix effect: which programs crash at compile time and which fail verification changed upstream with c8bc25a6d0 'Upgrade ASM to 9.11.1' (after 2.13.18).
links: CF2 / retronym/scala#618 (same genReturn cause). #618 is on w4-int (ed7156b3b3) and states it does not fix this form: it only spills the try's own result around a finalizer containing a return, and names try { foo(1, return 2) } finally ... and scala/bug#10183 as out of scope. A separate pull request for scala/bug#10183, not a wider #618.
note: The WP5 program is lrytz's minimization in scala/bug#10183 (open since 2017). The finding's on_2_13_18 'different' is input-dependent, not a difference in the defect: ASM 9.11 detects the inconsistent frame for some shapes and lets others through to the verifier, and ASM 9.9 the reverse, so neither build is better.
